subject: Ownership & fallback routing: training exclusion, outputs, and subprocessor sourcing
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@medbridge.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedBridge AI Legal <legal@medbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify training-exclusion + output ownership for EU patient sessions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team found the latency/cost profile promising. Before procurement can sign, our privacy counsel needs clarity on two related items for the pilot (EU residency):

1) Training exclusion: we require a firm "no-model-improve" commitment for session-scoped interactions (pilot patients). Is Redwood able to contractually commit that these sessions and any derived prompt/response content will never be used to tune models (even internally) and will be excluded from telemetry/telemetry-derived de-identified corpora?

2) Outputs & derivative ownership: MedBridge needs to confirm that generated responses (including multi-turn chat transcripts and structured outputs) are tenant-owned, and that Redwood will not assert derivative rights or use them as training seeds.

Separately, we need an operational fallback if our EU region experiences cross-border constraints — specifically: a subprocessor sourcing plan that ensures we can route to an onshore SFTP + onshore KMS or provide a contractual commitment to keep EU-resident sessions within EU. Can you share the current subprocessor list and a proposal for a failover path (SFTP push vs API egress) that meets our DPA requirements?

Can you send a redline or short statement we can attach to our DPA/PO? We need something concise for legal (1–2 paragraphs) plus an ops note on how the routing/fallback would work.

Appreciate it — Claire

Claire Zhou
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Interim)
MedBridge AI

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@medbridge.ai>
Cc: MedBridge AI Legal <legal@medbridge.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training-exclusion + output ownership for EU patient sessions

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes, we can contractually commit to session-scoped training exclusion and tenant ownership of generated outputs for the pilot; we have two standard operational paths for EU residency and an SFTP fallback option.

I'll loop in David (privacy counsel) for the two-paragraph contractual language and Kimberly (ops) for the technical failover/runbook. I'm attaching a DPA redline (DPA_draft_redlines_v2.docx) and our current subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_list.csv) for your review.

Next steps we propose:
- David to provide succinct redline language you can paste into the DPA (24–48h).
- Kimberly to outline the SFTP push vs API egress tradeoffs and an ops SLA for failover (48–72h).
- We'll mark session traffic with an "EU_NO_TRAIN" tag in metadata so it is excluded from telemetry and any downstream corpora.

Will follow up by EOD with the internal owners.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify training-exclusion + output ownership for EU patient sessions

Team — forwarding Claire's ask (see original below). TL;DR: MedBridge needs a contractual no-training commitment for sessions flagged as EU pilot, tenant ownership of outputs, and an operational fallback that keeps EU-resident sessions onshore or pushes to an SFTP on MedBridge's side.

Specific asks for legal/ops:
- Legal: two-paragraph redline that covers (a) absolute prohibition on using session data for model training or improvement; (b) explicit tenant ownership of generated outputs (chat transcripts, structured payloads, reranks). Include a clause that prohibits derivative-licensing and states Redwood will not use outputs as seeds for internal corpora.
- Ops: a short runbook describing the failover modes we can offer:
  * Preferred: geo-routing to EU pool (EU region GPU serving) with onshore KMS and storage.
  * Fallback A: TLS-pushed SFTP to MedBridge SFTP endpoint (they will provide creds) with immediate deletion from Redwood ephemeral caches.
  * Fallback B: API egress to an EU-certified partner, with contractual assurances around KMS residency.
- Technical gating: we need to ensure which subprocessors touch KV cache / telemetry (session logs, sampling) and whether those subprocessors are onshore in EU. Also include an assertion that any telemetry used for production monitoring will be anonymized and excluded from model corpora.

Deliverables & timeline: legal draft by Thu 08 Oct 2027 EOD; ops runbook draft by Fri 09 Oct 2027 EOD. Claire — we'll share both as soon as ready.

Thanks,
Rachel

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@medbridge.ai>, MedBridge AI Legal <legal@medbridge.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify training-exclusion + output ownership for EU patient sessions

Rachel / Kimberly — draft language below that should be suitable for insertion into the DPA (suggested redline). I kept it short for MedBridge legal's review.

--- PROPOSED REDLINE (to be inserted into Section X - Use of Customer Data) ---
1) No-Model-Improve Commitment: For any requests clearly marked by Customer metadata as "EU_NO_TRAIN" or otherwise designated in writing as subject to this clause, Redwood Inference shall not use, copy, retain, or incorporate the request content, associated prompts, or generated outputs for the purpose of training, fine-tuning, benchmarking, or otherwise improving any models, internal corpora, or training datasets. Redwood shall ensure such traffic is excluded from telemetry or aggregated corpora used for model development.

2) Output Ownership: Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to outputs generated in response to Customer requests (including multi-turn transcripts, structured payloads, and reranking results). Redwood covenants not to claim derivative rights, nor to license, redistribute, or derive commercial models from such outputs.

3) Subprocessor Sourcing & Failover: Redwood will maintain an up-to-date subprocessor inventory and, for EU-designated traffic, will route requests to EU-resident subprocessors and EU-region serving pools. In the event of sustained cross-border constraints, Redwood will support one of the following failover options: (a) TLS push to Customer-managed SFTP endpoint with immediate purge from Redwood ephemeral caches; (b) API egress to a mutually agreed EU-certified partner; or (c) switch to Customer-provided on-prem connector. Details for failover will be documented in an operational runbook.

--- end redline ---

Two operational notes: we should add a short paragraph saying "Redwood will flag EU_NO_TRAIN sessions in monitoring streams and will provide an attestation on request that flagged sessions were excluded from training corpora." Also confirm which subprocessors access KV cache or telemetry — Kimberly, can you confirm or point to the line in subprocessor_list.csv?

I'll sign off on this and can send to Claire as a redline attachment.

-David

David Kim
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify training-exclusion + output ownership for EU patient sessions

Rachel / David — thank you, that redline looks good and addresses counsel's main asks. A few quick clarifications before we move to contract:

- The "attestation on request" wording is acceptable; can we add a delivery SLA (e.g., attestation within 5 business days)?
- For the SFTP fallback: we'll take TLS push to our SFTP and provide credentials. Please confirm the deletion timeline on Redwood side (we expect immediate purge from ephemeral caches and deletion from any backup within 24 hours).

If you can provide a DocuSign-ready redline and the SFTP technical contact + sample runbook snippet, we can route to procurement. Otherwise, please send a DocuSign link and we'll sign the DPA addendum.

Claire

Claire Zhou
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Interim)
